flow_breaks.detail: Ghidra's stored function body is 004e4a40-004e4a47 only; the decompiler traverses the whole routine and the export is complete. Recorded in reports/game_onmove_body_repair.json. Not touched by this packet.

The export opens with 'Removing unreachable block (ram,0x004e5455)' and '(ram,0x004e5460)'. The listing shows a real do/while: 006840f0 writes a bool into [esp+0x1B], 004e5453 branches on it, and the body runs 00776230 (ECX game+0x1EF0) then 004c40f0, clears the flag and re-polls, looping while the flag is set. Ghidra cannot see the write through the pointer argument, so it proves the branch always taken. 00776230 appears in the call graph but in no line of pseudocode.
The real body is 2808 bytes, not the 4352 dumped. int3 padding starts at 004e5538. The two RETs are ret 4 at 004e4b8c and ret 4 at 004e5535; the six pseudocode return statements share them.

Tagged STL_xlen_throw but called with three arguments (auStack_14, list head, node) from the erase point of the game+0x5BC walk when the node's float timer at +0x14 expires. The classification and the call shape disagree.
About twenty call sites are 'call getter; mov ecx,eax; call method'; the pseudocode renders these as two unrelated zero-argument calls. Every ECX in this report came from the listing.
BSP_GuiManager_GetOrCreate(1), FUN_00425d10(uVar6) and FUN_004f71f0(uVar6) show arguments the listing does not push.

A DAT_0109cefc vtable+4 call is compared against 0x3200000 (50 MiB) and the only effect is storing -1 into the SEH try-level slot at [esp+0x40]. The guarded body appears optimised away; do not read it as a working memory check.
The 5.60519e-45 literal passed to BSP_Game_EnqueueStateRequest is the integer 4 reinterpreted; the particle step reads DAT_00f876a4 * qword [0xce47a0] on x87 and truncates to float.
All 95 indexed callees were confirmed against the listing and the listing contains no target the index lacks. For this function the pseudocode is the lossy view, not the index.

packets.contract: Produce the scaled delta at game+0x21F0 and the global clock at DAT_01090AB0+4 from the raw OnMove argument, and drain the state-request ring at game+0x5E0..+0x5EC into the next frame's game+0x5D4.
The input singleton's per-frame poll and the two timed effect lists at game+0x5B0 and game+0x5BC, including the node-erase path through 004d11d0.
The loading/modal fast path that renders GUI only and returns at 004e4b8c, plus the GUI enable and disable pair. Smallest packet that yields a frame the game can run.
States 1, 2 and 4 including the DAT_00f8abe8+1000 GUI branch and the render tail all three share.

Per-frame platform notification, online-stats and multiplayer-session polling, plus the menu-interface request drain at 004e5455 that must be reconstructed from the listing because the decompiler removed it.
The state-0x0D entry condition, the pause-key gate and its two branches: open the pause menu, or switch the audio environment and run the interface-only update.
The 0xA0-byte tracker singleton and its seven update passes with their unit-class, weapon and *1STGET string tables.
The entity, marker, decal, bot and mission-event updates driven from game+0x21F0 with ECX taken from game+0x21A0, +0x21D0 and +0x21D4.
The game+0x19E8 ocean and game+0x19FC effect updates plus the game+0x1EE7 one-shot that arms them.

Everything between the last simulation call and BSP_Game_Render: the particle step, terrain and listener binding, and the front-end root update. Render-queue globals stay read-only because main:frame_bounds_integration owns them.
